area_summary:
The renderer's slot accounting is careful: removed flags prevent double-release, capture is released when a drop is removed, and the TTS double play is already guarded by `spoke` (only an error in the middle of the server audio could re-speak text, which is negligible). On Windows software compositing, though, two avoidable things dominate the per-frame cost while a drop is on screen. The first is the drop-shadow filters on the animated .drop, which are recomputed every frame. The second is the rAF spotlight, which repaints a full-screen gradient every frame.

**Measured CPU.** Setup: Playwright Chromium with --disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing, 1920x1080, one 700x500 image drop, Windows defaults, 4 vCPU Xeon 2.1 GHz.
- Today: about 1150 ms of CPU per second at only about 12 fps, roughly 94 ms of CPU per frame.
- With the shadow fix and the spotlight fix: 630-750 ms/s at 60 fps, about 10-12 ms per frame.
- A frozen drop costs 0 in both versions.
- What remains is the always-on bob and life bar, which are part of the design (on Windows each frame also means a full-window layered update).

**Idle cost.**
- The AudioContext is never suspended: after the first pop it causes about 230 wakeups/s forever.
- The Android shim runs an 8 Hz timer even with no drop on screen.
- In main.js, `forward:true` installs a global low-level mouse hook that the renderer never uses (cross-component finding).

**Verified bugs.**
- Exit animations are invisible.
- The spotlight veil darkens the meme itself.
- Caption size depends on load timing and the entry effect.
- With overlapping drops, the bottom one is grabbed, and every mousemove churns the hover class.
- Audio drops that never load leak their slots and block the queue.
- Media are only paused on removal, so a closed video keeps downloading.
- Live settings are lost for playing and queued videos.
- On Windows, large memes can spawn with the close button off-screen.
- A second shake within 700 ms is lost.
- Rain is unbounded.

Each item was checked in headless Chromium with a stub bridge, and a prototype patch with all fixes passes the same tests. Everything is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-memedrop/065ca17e-4939-5472-b348-276c03e80469/scratchpad/audit-scratch/overlay-r/: overlay-opt.js/.html, android-shim-opt.js, perf3.js and perf5.js (CPU and fps bench), t1-t14 (bug repros), spot-test*.png and vis-*.png (screenshots). No project file was modified.

findings.title: filter: drop-shadow on the animated .drop is recomputed every frame (bob + life-bar)
findings.evidence: .drop (overlay.html:57-59) has filter: drop-shadow(0 30px 60px ...) drop-shadow(0 6px 12px ...) plus an infinite drop-bob; the life-bar inside also changes every frame. A filter forces a render surface whose content changes each frame, so both Gaussian blurs are recomputed on the CPU every frame under software compositing. Measured (Playwright Chromium, --disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing, 1920x1080, one 700x500 image drop, 4 vCPU Xeon 2.1 GHz): 74-94 ms CPU per frame and only 12-13 fps; same drop frozen = 0 ms/s; shadow as box-shadow: 9-12 ms/frame at 60 fps. Today fx-zoom also shows no shadow until ~390 ms (discrete blur->drop-shadow flip, sampled) and fx-glitch drops it for ~720 ms.
findings.behavior_change: visible: near-identical shadow (mean alpha diff 1.9/255, max 31 next to the avatar); the shadow no longer pops in late during fx-zoom nor disappears during fx-glitch
findings.cross_component: none (overlay.html is copied into the APK by syncWebAssets; on Android it also removes a per-frame GPU blur)
findings.risk: Low: pure CSS; the drop layer gets larger bounds (rasterized once). Compare side by side on a real Windows box once.
findings.value: ~6-8x less CPU per frame while any drop is visible on Windows (software compositing); restores 60 fps instead of ~12 fps; cheaper on Android GPU too.

findings.title: Spotlight rAF loop forces layout and repaints a full-screen gradient every frame
findings.evidence: tickSpotlight (overlay.js:358-378) runs every frame while a spotlighted drop is connected (spotlightOnDrop defaults to true on Windows): getBoundingClientRect forces style+layout, then 4 setProperty on #spotlight. drop-bob moves/rotates that rect every frame, so the values always change and the full-screen radial-gradient (overlay.html:404-416) is re-rasterized every frame. Measured with the box-shadow CSS: rAF spotlight 23-26 ms CPU/frame vs 10-12 ms with an event-driven spotlight (spotlight off: 9-11). Prototype checked: hole follows media load (ResizeObserver), drag, __mdDropCtl.move, window resize, switches to the next drop and turns off on removal.
findings.behavior_change: visible (minor): the hole stays on the drop's resting position instead of following the +-6px/0.6deg bob and the entry/exit motion; it still updates on media load, drag, Android move and resize
findings.risk: Low: ResizeObserver exists since Chromium 64 (WebView >= 80) and is guarded; offset* values equal today's rect when the drop is at rest.
findings.value: Removes a forced layout plus a full-screen repaint every frame while the spotlight is on (Windows default); about halves per-frame CPU once the shadow fix is in.

findings.title: Exit animations never show: drops and toasts vanish instantly
findings.evidence: @keyframes drop-out/drop-close-out (overlay.html:381-386) and audio-out (395-397) only define `to`. When .leaving/.closing replaces the animation list, drop-in (fill forwards) is cancelled, so the implicit 0% keyframe uses the base style: .drop {opacity:0, no transform} (line 60) and .audio-toast {opacity:0}. Sampled computed opacity every frame in Chromium: 0.00 from the very first frame of .leaving, .closing and .audio-toast.leaving; the designed 380 ms fall and 220/280 ms fades are never visible. Also mousedown sets inline animationPlayState='paused' (overlay.js:119) and removeNow (810) clears dragState but not that style, so an exit started mid-drag stays paused (verified).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): drops fall/fade out and audio/TTS toasts slide out as the CSS comments describe
findings.cross_component: none (Android shim already drops .leaving/.closing drops from the touch rects)
findings.risk: Very low: the start pose jumps at most 6px/0.6deg (bob), more only if closed mid-entry; existing timers (220/400/300 ms) already cover the durations.
findings.value: Restores the intended exit UX on both platforms.

findings.title: Spotlight veil is painted over the meme and darkens its edges
findings.evidence: #spotlight has z-index:1 (overlay.html:407) while #stage, which holds the drops, is z-index:auto, so the veil is painted ON TOP of the meme. Its gradient is transparent only inside 35% of radii (w/2+70, h/2+70), so the meme's edges and corners get darkened. Pixel test in Chromium (700x500 grey image, value 200): spotlight on -> 30px inside the top-left corner = 44 (~78% black), 30px inside the left edge = 101, centre 200. spotlightOnDrop defaults to true on Windows, so every meme is vignetted, contrary to the comment 'un trou transparent centré sur le drop'. With z-index:0 those pixels stay 200 (veil painted before #stage in DOM order).
findings.proposed_change:
overlay.html #spotlight: replace `z-index: 1;` by
  z-index: 0;   /* sous #stage (ordre du DOM) : le voile entoure le mème sans l'assombrir */
Rain (z 9999) and audio toasts (z 999) stay above. Before/after screenshots: scratch overlay-r/spot-test.png vs spot-test-z0.png.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): the meme is no longer darkened at its edges/corners; the darkening around it is unchanged
findings.risk: Very low (one CSS value); trivially revertible if the vignette was intended.
findings.value: Correct spotlight look; also slightly cheaper per frame (measured 10.3 vs 12.3 ms/frame).

findings.title: Shared AudioContext stays running forever after the first pop
findings.evidence: popCtx (overlay.js:135-157) is created at the first pop and stays 'running' for the life of the page (only recreated if closed). A running AudioContext keeps the WebAudio render thread ticking even when silent. Measured in headless Chromium after one pop, page otherwise idle: ~14 ms CPU/s and ~230 voluntary context switches/s, indefinitely; after popCtx.suspend(): 0 ms/s and ~2/s. The Windows overlay renderer lives 24/7 and soundOnArrival defaults to true, so this runs from the first drop until the app quits (on Android until the WebView is destroyed after 90 s idle), and keeps an audio output stream open.
findings.behavior_change: none (the pop may start a few tens of ms later after a resume)
findings.risk: Low: both hosts already allow audio without a gesture (Electron default policy, WebView mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture=false), which the current code relies on.
findings.value: Removes a permanent ~230 Hz wakeup source from an always-on process on gaming PCs (and an open audio stream on phones).

findings.title: Audio drop that never loads keeps its toast and slot forever
findings.evidence: playAudioDrop frees its slot only through 'ended', 'error', play().catch or timeupdate >= 10 s (overlay.js:536-541). A URL that never answers or a stalled connection raises none of them (play() stays pending), so the toast stays and `active` is never decremented. Videos have a 15 s guard (693-695) and images a timer; audio has nothing. Verified with a request that never responds: 6 audio drops -> after 40 s still 6 toasts, active=6, and a later image drop stays in dropQueue forever (MAX_CONCURRENT reached).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: a stuck audio toast disappears after 25 s and its slot is freed
findings.risk: Very low: normal audio drops end at <= 10 s.
findings.value: Prevents a permanently blocked queue and stuck toasts after network hiccups.

findings.title: Removed media are only paused: a closed video keeps downloading
findings.evidence: On removal, videos (overlay.js:807), music (813-816) and audio drops (523) are only paused, and the TTS <audio> (300-305) is never released. A paused element keeps src, decoder, buffers and its HTTP connection until GC, which can be late in a mostly idle renderer. Verified with a throttled local server: a video drop closed 1.5 s after arrival kept downloading the whole file afterwards (464 KB -> 2140 KB, connection still open 6 s later); with src removed + load() the client closed the connection 220 ms after the close. On Android that means mobile data and radio time for every early close, 15 s load timeout or skipped video.
findings.risk: Low: load() without src only fires 'emptied' and a timeupdate at t=0; existing error/ended handlers are guarded by removed flags and the cap checks never trigger at 0.
findings.value: Deterministic release of decoders/buffers/sockets; stops wasted downloads (notably Android mobile data).

findings.title: Caption size computed from the transformed width during the entry animation
findings.evidence: fitCaption uses mediaEl.getBoundingClientRect().width (overlay.js:438), which includes the .drop entry transform (drop-in starts at scale(.6) rotate(-8deg), fx-zoom at scale(3.2), fx-tornade at scale(.05)). When the media is cached or loads fast (replays, same meme twice, fast CDN) the measure happens mid-animation. Verified with a cached 300x400 image (expected 27px): 19px with no effect, 40px with zoom, 13px with tornade; 200x300 image (expected 18px): 13px, zoom 40px.
findings.proposed_change: overlay.js:438 -> `const w = mediaEl.offsetWidth;   // largeur de mise en page (hors transform d'entrée)`. Same 0-before-load semantics, so the load/loadedmetadata/rAF retry logic is unchanged. Prototype: 27px/18px in every effect case.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): caption size is consistently 9% of the displayed media width whatever the load timing or entry effect

findings.title: Hover/drag picks the bottom drop; hover class toggled on every mousemove
findings.evidence: findDropAt (overlay.js:40-51) walks stage.querySelectorAll('.anchor') in DOM order and returns the first hit, i.e. the OLDEST drop, while newer drops paint on top: with two overlapping drops the hovered/dragged one is the bottom one (verified; elementFromPoint gives the top one). The mousemove handler then tests `hit !== hoveredDrop` (line 100), but findDropAt returns a fresh object every call, so it is always true: each mousemove over the same drop removes and re-adds .hover (verified: 20 class mutations for 10 moves). Each call also costs ~200 us median with 6 drops (getBoundingClientRect forces an animation style update).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): with overlapping drops the visible top drop is the one hovered and dragged
findings.value: Correct grabbing; no style invalidation per mousemove.

findings.title: Android shim polls drop rects every 120 ms even with no drop on screen
findings.evidence: setInterval(reportRects, 120) (android-shim.js:88) starts at page load and runs as long as the overlay WebView exists (OverlayController keeps it 90 s after the last drop, indefinitely while drops keep coming): 8.3 wakeups/s doing querySelectorAll + JSON.stringify with nothing on screen. overlay.js already calls window.memedrop.watchCursor() when the first visual drop appears and unwatchCursor() after the last one is removed (overlay.js:338-348); the shim maps both to noop (lines 18-19). Verified with a mocked MDOverlay: idle ticks 17 per 2 s today vs 0, rects still sent while a drop is shown and an empty list after it leaves.
findings.behavior_change: none (only the useless empty-list message at page load disappears; native starts with no handles)
findings.cross_component: none (relies on overlay.js onVisualDropAdded/Removed, unchanged; MDOverlay.rects JSON format unchanged)
findings.value: No timer wakeups on the phone while no drop is visible.

findings.title: setIgnoreMouseEvents forward:true keeps a global low-level mouse hook that the renderer never uses
findings.evidence: main.js:199 and :797 keep the overlay in setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true }) permanently. On Windows Electron implements forward with a global WH_MOUSE_LL hook on the browser UI thread and re-posts each WM_MOUSEMOVE to the overlay, which dispatches a DOM mousemove to the renderer (native_window_views_win.cc SetForwardMouseMessages; ~80% sure unchanged in Electron 33). The renderer never uses those events: overlay.js:84-85 returns at once when !inCapture, hover detection uses the polled overlay:cursor IPC, and in capture mode setIgnoreMouseEvents(false) delivers events normally. So every mouse event of the game (1000 Hz gaming mice) transits through Electron 24/7 for nothing.
findings.proposed_change: main.js:199 -> `overlayWin.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);` and main.js:797 -> `overlayWin.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);` (cursor polling unchanged). Update the comments that mention forward:true (overlay.html:213-215, main.js:757-763). Manual check on Windows: hover -> capture -> drag/close/react still work (they rely only on the polled cursor and on normal events while capturing).
findings.behavior_change: none (renderer logic unchanged; :hover state is refreshed by the real mousemove that triggers exitCapture)
findings.cross_component: overlay/src/overlay.js (no change needed: its DOM mousemove handler is gated on inCapture); outside the renderer files, report here because the renderer contract is what makes it safe
findings.risk: Low-medium: Electron-internals premise (~80% confidence) and needs one manual test on Windows.
findings.value: Removes a system-wide low-level mouse hook plus a renderer wakeup per mouse move, 24/7, on gamers' PCs.

findings.title: Live settings changes are reverted or ignored for playing videos and queued drops
findings.evidence: (a) The video's 'canplay'/'play' handlers (overlay.js:680-681) re-apply the drop's const initialVideoVol (663); 'canplay' fires again after every rebuffer, so a live volume change (880) is silently reverted. (b) videoMaxSec is const (647): rescheduleFor (832-855) re-times the removal, but timeupdate (682-687) and a not-yet-fired loadedmetadata (670-679) still use the old cap, so raising 'durée max vidéo' live never lets a playing video run longer. (c) Payloads waiting in dropQueue keep the settings snapshot from their arrival, so volume/durations/opacity/spotlight changed meanwhile are ignored when they are finally shown.
findings.proposed_change: (a) video branch: `el._mdVol = settings?.volume ?? 0.75;   // volume courant, suivi en direct` + `const reapplyVol = () => applyVolume(el, el._mdVol);` and use reapplyVol instead of the 4 applyVolume(el, initialVideoVol) calls; onSettingsUpdate: `for (const p of livePlayables) { p._mdVol = settings.volume; applyVolume(p, settings.volume); }`. (b) `let videoMaxSec = ...` and at the top of rescheduleFor: `if (dropMeta.kind === 'video') videoMaxSec = newCapSec;`. (c) first line of the onSettingsUpdate callback: `for (const q of dropQueue) q.settings = { ...q.settings, ...settings };   // la file joue avec les réglages à jour` (Windows sends only changed keys, Android the full set: both merge correctly).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: live volume/duration changes stick for playing videos and apply to queued drops
findings.value: Settings sliders behave as users expect.

findings.title: On Windows a large meme can spawn partly off-screen with its close button unreachable
findings.evidence: chooseSpot keeps the centre within 14-86% x / 20-80% y, but media can be 38vw x 50vh (plus the avatar ~31px above), so a drop can overflow by ~5vw/5vh. clampCenter/__mdDropCtl.fit (overlay.js:177-200) only run on Android, where android-shim.js calls fit every 120 ms (fix 287abbd 'croix accessible'). Verified at 1920x1080 with a 1600x1200 image: Math.random=0 -> media at (-93,-61) and close button at y -63..-45 (off-screen); Math.random~1 -> close button at x 1999..2017.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): a large meme near an edge shifts inward once its size is known (same as the APK)
findings.cross_component: none (Android shim keeps its periodic fit)
findings.value: Close button always reachable on Windows.

findings.title: Second 'shake' drop within 700 ms is cut short or lost
findings.evidence: effect 'shake' (overlay.js:590-592) adds body.fx-shake and removes it 700 ms later with an untracked timer. If a second shake drop arrives within 700 ms, classList.add is a no-op (the animation does not restart) and the first timer removes the class early, so the second shake is truncated or lost.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix (visible): every shake drop shakes fully

findings.title: Emoji rain bypasses the concurrency/queue limits (spam vector)
findings.evidence: MAX_CONCURRENT/MAX_QUEUE only gate media drops (overlay.js:552-555). Rain-only drops (561-566) and the rain of every media drop call renderRain without any bound: 38 elements with will-change (38 composited layers) and 38 timers per rain, alive ~5.3 s. Several friends using /drop pluie (bot cooldown 2 s per sender) or /dropall can stack hundreds of layers on one target's gaming PC or phone, the very spam MAX_QUEUE was added against.
findings.behavior_change: visible only under spam: a 5th simultaneous rain is skipped (the drop itself still shows)
findings.value: Bounds worst-case CPU/memory from spam; 1 timer per rain instead of 38.
